capstone-grounded-cited-rag.text: Every earlier lesson built one primitive: chunking, embeddings, cosine, top-k, the threshold gate, grounding, citations, refusal, recall@k, faithfulness. Production needs them working TOGETHER on one request — a retrieval that clears (or fails) the threshold, a grounded and cited answer (or an honest refusal), and an evaluation of the whole run. This capstone wires them into one pipeline and proves the composition is correct on both an answerable and an unanswerable query.

A production RAG request is a small pipeline, not a single call: score chunks by cosine and take the top-k; check the top score against the threshold τ and REFUSE if nothing clears it; otherwise ground the answer by mapping claims to supporting chunks and CITE each with its source+span; and, for evaluation, compute recall@k against the labeled relevant set and faithfulness against the retrieved context. This capstone composes the course's primitives into that path and runs a scripted scenario end to end — proving the whole is correct, not just the parts.

capstone-grounded-cited-rag.prompt: Before reading: list the course primitives a single grounded, cited, evaluated RAG request must combine.
capstone-grounded-cited-rag.reveal: Cosine ranking + top-k (retrieve), the threshold/refusal gate (decide answer vs refuse), grounding (claims -> supporting chunks) and citation (source+span per claim), and the two metrics — recall@k (retrieval) and faithfulness (generation). The capstone is not new material; it is the correct COMPOSITION of these into one path with a run report.

capstone-grounded-cited-rag.intro: The pipeline as a sequence over the course primitives, producing an answer-or-refusal plus a run report.
steps: Rank candidates by cosine and take the top-k (retrieval stage).
Gate on τ: if the best chunk is below threshold, REFUSE — do not fabricate.
Otherwise ground: keep chunks clearing τ and cite each claim to a source+span.
Evaluate the run: recall@k (retrieval) and faithfulness (generation) in one report.
capstone-grounded-cited-rag.commonMistake: Wiring the primitives but skipping the gate on the answerable path — grounding and citing without ever checking τ, so an unanswerable query slips through and gets a fabricated, "cited" answer. The gate must sit BETWEEN retrieval and grounding, exactly the failure the threshold lesson warned about, resurfacing in composition.

capstone-grounded-cited-rag.text: Everything the course taught converges into one request path, and the discipline is COMPOSITION. Model the request as a small pipeline: RETRIEVE (score candidates by cosine, take the top-k), GATE (compare the top score to the threshold τ; if nothing clears it, refuse honestly rather than ground on noise), GROUND + CITE (on the answerable path, keep the chunks clearing τ, map each answer claim to a supporting chunk, and attach a source+span citation — dropping any claim you cannot cite), and EVALUATE (compute recall@k against the labeled relevant set to score retrieval, and faithfulness against the retrieved context to score generation). Each stage is a primitive you already built and tested in isolation; the capstone proves they fit together without dropping a concern — the gate actually guards grounding, every grounded claim actually carries a citation, and the metrics actually measure the path that ran. The output is a RUN REPORT: the action taken (answer or refuse), the citations, and the two eval numbers. That report is the "proof, not vibes" artifact for the whole course — it shows an answerable query producing a grounded, cited answer with high recall and faithfulness, AND an unanswerable query producing an honest refusal, on the same pipeline. Build RAG this way: not as a lucky single retrieve-and-generate, but as an explicit, observable pipeline over primitives you can each defend, with an evaluation attached so quality is a measured number and refusal is a designed outcome.

storyboard.say: A production RAG request enters as a pipeline: first score every candidate chunk by cosine and keep the top-k with their scores.
The top-k and their scores flow into the threshold gate, the one decision that separates an answerable request from noise.
If the top score clears tau, we proceed to ground the answer on the chunks that passed.
If nothing clears tau, we refuse honestly rather than fabricate an answer on weak evidence.
On the answerable path we map each claim to a supporting chunk, cite its source and span, and drop any claim we cannot back.
The grounded answer plus its retrieved context flows into evaluation, the audit stage.
Eval emits a run report: recall@k scores retrieval, faithfulness scores generation against the context.
Every primitive you built converges into one path; the discipline that makes it production-grade is composition.

capstone-grounded-cited-rag.guidance: Compose (A). The course deliberately built each primitive alone so the capstone is composition, not new logic — that is what makes it testable, what surfaces a skipped gate as an obvious missing stage, and what lets the same primitives power the next RAG feature. The monolith (B) is exactly how the "grounded without gating" bug slips in.

capstone-grounded-cited-rag.explanation: Correct composition means the stages actually connect: the gate guards grounding (so unanswerable queries refuse), grounded claims carry citations, and the eval measures the path that ran. Demonstrating both the answer path (grounded, cited, measured) and the refusal path on one pipeline is the proof — a fluent answer alone can hide a skipped gate.
